disclaimer: Free zone pricing is indicative and changes annually. Most zones no longer publish a licence tariff, so several figures in this pack are dated historical snapshots that could not be re-confirmed on 2026-10-13 (see each record's price_status and price_note). Verify with the official free zone website or a written quotation before quoting figures to a founder; visa, premises, establishment card and service fees are usually extra.
renewal_note: Renewal fees depend on the zone, activity, premises, visa package and any introductory subsidy. Do not infer a universal renewal percentage from the indicative historical prices in this pack.

freezone_to_mainland.name: Free Zone Mainland Operating Permit
freezone_to_mainland.legislation: Dubai Executive Council Resolution No. 11 of 2025
freezone_to_mainland.status: Operational. Under Resolution 11 of 2025 DET may issue a branch licence within the Emirate, a licence for a branch operating out of the free zone, or a temporary permit. On 8 October 2025 DET (DBLC) and the Dubai Free Zones Council launched the Free Zone Mainland Operating Permit (the temporary-permit route) for eligible free zone companies holding a Dubai Unified Licence. No DET or Dubai Media Office update to the permit terms was found between that launch and 2026-10-13.
freezone_to_mainland.apply_via: Invest in Dubai platform (fully digital application; requires a Dubai Unified Licence)

permit_types.period: 1 year, renewable for the same period
permit_types.fee_note: Article 5 licence for a branch within the Emirate: the Resolution sets no amount; prescribed DET fees apply under applicable legislation. Obtain a DET quote.

permit_types.period: 1 year, renewable for the same period
permit_types.fee_note: Article 12(1): AED 10,000 per year to issue or renew a licence for a branch operating out of the free zone.

permit_types.period: up to 6 months, renewable at the same fee
permit_types.fee_note: Article 12(2): AED 5,000 to issue or renew. Marketed by DET as the Free Zone Mainland Operating Permit (6 months, AED 5,000).

freezone_to_mainland.phase_one_scope: Per the 8 October 2025 DET launch, the Operating Permit's initial phase covers non-regulated activities (technology, consultancy, design, professional services, trading). Regulated sectors are planned for a later phase; no extension to regulated sectors had been announced as of 2026-10-13.
freezone_to_mainland.regularisation_status: Article 13 required existing free zone establishments conducting activity in mainland Dubai to regularise within one year from the Resolution's effective date. Article 15 made the Resolution effective on publication in Official Gazette issue 707, published 21 March 2025 (re-checked 2026-10-13), producing a 21 March 2026 deadline; some law-firm commentary uses the 3 March 2025 issue date instead. The Director General may grant one extension for the same period where necessary; no public DET announcement of an extension was found as of 2026-10-13, and this pack does not assert that an extension is automatic or that a particular establishment received one. Confirm current status with DET before relying on the deadline.
freezone_to_mainland.tax_note: Keep separate financial records for mainland activities. DET's launch statement says related mainland revenue is subject to 9% corporate tax; the exact treatment still depends on QFZP status, income classification and any domestic permanent establishment, so do not assume every dirham of mainland-sourced revenue is taxed the same way.
freezone_to_mainland.excluded_entities: Article 2: the Resolution does not apply to financial establishments licensed to operate in the DIFC.

developments_2026.headline: District IO innovation district launched at DSO/DIEZ (AED 12.8bn expansion)
developments_2026.summary: AED 12.8 billion of expansion projects for Dubai Silicon Oasis under DIEZ, launched by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid on 22 January 2026. District IO (AED 11bn; reported as 25 LEED-compliant buildings, 18 commercial; phase one office, R&D and retail in 2026, phase two hospitality and innovation facilities in 2027) targets smart mobility, 3D printing, robotics, AI, quantum, Web3 and X-Tech, with incentives including end-to-end setup, funding support, flexible leasing and RegLab product testing. Block 14 (AED 1.8bn, transit-oriented development near the Metro Blue Line) completes 2029. Building counts differ slightly between outlets.

developments_2026.headline: Meydan launches fully remote non-residency setup with a guaranteed corporate account via MPlus
developments_2026.summary: Fully remote company formation: founders anywhere can obtain a UAE trade licence online in as little as 60 minutes (24 hours for complex structures) across 2,500+ activities, then open a corporate bank account via Meydan's MPlus banking team (26+ banking partners, up to 17 currencies) without travelling to the UAE. Marketed as a guaranteed bank account with the licence.
developments_2026.caveat: Originally a single-source Gulf News company-news item. On 2026-10-13 Meydan's official launch page listed a Non-Resident Licence at AED 12,500, confirming the remote-setup product, but the guaranteed-bank-account claim was not confirmed on an official Meydan page; treat it as marketing.

developments_2026.headline: Dubai South announces 2026 incentive package
developments_2026.summary: Dubai South's newsroom lists three incentives: support for new company formation, facilitation of licence renewals, and exemption from late-renewal fines, framed under the Dubai Free Zones Council's competitiveness push. No financial terms, eligibility rules or end date are published; eligibility is checked case by case via 800 SOUTH.

developments_2026.headline: DMCC crosses 26,000 members and signs a Tether MoU
developments_2026.summary: DMCC signed an MoU with Tether covering blockchain and payment infrastructure within DMCC, tokenisation advisory and ecosystem programmes. DMCC reports 26,000+ member companies including 4,000+ tech firms; the Crypto Centre crossed 700 members (38% YoY growth). DMCC also announced a Crypto.com commodities-tokenisation partnership and launched DMCC Quantum in H1 2026.

developments_2026.headline: Al Selmiyyah Defence Industrial Free Zone announced in Abu Dhabi (outside Dubai)
developments_2026.summary: Tawazun Council and AD Ports Group announced a defence industrial free zone in Abu Dhabi aimed at global defence OEMs, domestic production, technology transfer and SME participation in defence supply chains, under the Operation 300bn industrial strategy. No size, timeline or investment figures disclosed yet. Outside Dubai; noted for completeness only and not part of the Dubai zone matrix.

developments_2026.headline: DIEZ launches temporary economic relief measures for DAFZ, DSO and Dubai CommerCity
developments_2026.summary: Announced via the Dubai Media Office: rent held stable at contract renewal, waiver of certain administrative penalties including late licence renewal fines, monthly rent instalments with instalment fees waived, three-month deferral of shareholder-amendment and activity-amendment fees, and waiver of restructuring and authorised-capital amendment fees. Linked to Dubai's AED 1 billion facilitation package (from 1 April 2026 for three to six months). Waivers run 'until conditions stabilise'; no end date or extension was found as of 2026-10-13, so confirm current status with DIEZ.

license.price_note: Re-checked 2026-10-13: IFZA's official Set Up Your Business page still publishes no licence price or visa tiers (consultation and tailored proposal only). The AED 12,900 / 12,500 figures are an unverified historical 2025-Q4 snapshot, not a current IFZA quote.

office.notes: IFZA's official setup page says virtual workplaces are allowed for some free zone companies; office solutions are set in the tailored proposal.

visas.tiers_described: Packages from 0 (zero-visa) up to 6 visas per 2025-Q4 market packages. IFZA's official pages do not publish tiers; unverified as of 2026-10-13.

banking.notes: Single-source consultancy report (July 2025) cites approximately 68% banking delays for IFZA setups. Treat as a prior, not a fact.

license.verified_note: Meydan's official launch page, re-checked 2026-10-13, advertises company formation from AED 12,500 per year (licence, registration, digital application, portal access and a flexi desk), a Fawri instant licence at AED 15,000, a Non-Resident Licence at AED 12,500, and up to 15% off multi-year licences. Visas, medical, Emirates ID and office upgrades are extra. Renewal at AED 12,500 is not separately confirmed.

office.notes: A flexi desk is bundled into every licence at no separate charge, so no separate physical lease is needed to start; office upgrades are add-ons.

visas.tiers_described: Base setup has 0 visa allocations; allocations are pay-as-you-go at AED 1,850 each, up to 6 per licence (Meydan official cost breakdown, updated 2026-06-30).

banking.notes: Most-cited problem zone for bank rejections. Meydan runs an in-house bank-assistance desk to mitigate. Use it before submitting applications to multiple banks.

license.notes: License from approximately AED 10,000. General Trading variant from approximately AED 20,000.
license.price_note: Not re-confirmable on an official page on 2026-10-13 (no published tariff); kept as an unverified historical snapshot dated 2025-Q4. Dubai South's official site publishes no licence prices (call-back form only); third-party package figures conflict.

banking.notes: Solid aviation/logistics positioning helps with bank acceptance for sector-aligned activities.

license.price_note: Not re-confirmable on an official page on 2026-10-13 (no published tariff); kept as an unverified historical snapshot dated 2025-Q4. DAFZ publishes no tariff; its homepage could not be read and consultancy estimates conflict widely.

banking.notes: Premium location and DAFZA brand carry weight with most banks.

free_zones.name: DSO / Dtec
free_zones.full_name: Dubai Silicon Oasis with Dtec coworking and incubation

license.notes: Cost varies by Dtec membership tier and licence package. Dtec's site lists hot desks, dedicated desks and private offices but did not expose prices on 2026-10-13; use Dtec's Plans and Pricing section or ask for a quote.

free_zones.name: TECOM (DIC, DMC, DKP)
free_zones.full_name: Dubai Internet City, Dubai Media City, Dubai Knowledge Park
free_zones.location: Sheikh Zayed Road, Knowledge Village area

license.notes: Pricing varies by business district and package. TECOM Group's setup page (re-checked 2026-10-13) publishes no prices and covers 10 districts: Dubai Internet City, Dubai Media City, Dubai Design District, Dubai Industrial City, Dubai Science Park, Dubai International Academic City, Dubai Knowledge Park, Dubai Studio City, Dubai Production City and Dubai Outsource City. Get a quote directly.

banking.notes: Established tech and media zones; banks are familiar with TECOM tenants.

license.notes: Basic license approximately AED 35,484 in year one. Per-visa fees are charged on top, so a 3-visa setup is materially higher than the headline figure.
license.official_range_note: DMCC's official set-up page, re-checked 2026-10-13, states initial setup costs typically range from AED 10,345 to AED 84,515 depending on licence duration and office space; registration takes about 10 working days. The AED 35,484 / 30,000 figures remain an unverified dated 2025-Q4 package snapshot.

office.notes: Options range from flexi-desks and serviced offices to private office space; every company needs a registered DMCC office address. Visa eligibility depends on office space and licence type.

visas.tiers_described: Visa quota is tied to office space and licence type (DMCC official set-up page, 2026-10-13). No fixed cap published.

banking.notes: Established free zone with broad bank familiarity. DUL coverage is Dubai-wide rather than a special programme limited to selected free zones.

free_zones.name: DIFC Innovation Licence
free_zones.full_name: Dubai International Financial Centre, Innovation Licence

license.subsidy_notes: DIFC's official page (re-checked 2026-10-20) states the licence is subsidised for 2 to 5 years at USD 1,500 per year. DIFC's Private Company, Non-Financial and Retail Handbook (DIFC-CS-GL-12 Rev.06, approved 29 September 2026) sets a USD 100 incorporation fee and a USD 1,500 annual Innovation Licence fee: discounted for the first 2 years for all entities, discounted in years 3 to 7 only for entities with 10 or fewer employees, and the normal USD 12,000 fee for entities with more than 10 employees from year 3 and for all entities from year 8. DIFC's Innovation Licence setup guide (January 2025) gives the taper for 10 or fewer full-time employees: USD 1,500 in years 1 to 5, USD 4,000 in year 6, USD 8,000 in year 7 and USD 12,000 from year 8. renewal_usd is that USD 12,000 normal fee, not the year-2 renewal for a small company.

office.notes: Applicants must procure space in DIFC after initial approval (official page). Flexi-desk minimum. No virtual-only setup.

visas.tiers_described: Up to 4 visas on the first desk and discounted visa costs, per DIFC's official Innovation Licence setup guide (January 2025, re-checked 2026-10-20); the web page only says visas are discounted. Visas beyond the first desk depend on additional DIFC space; confirm with DIFC.

banking.notes: Bank acceptance depends on the bank and applicant. No official acceptance rating is published for this zone.

restrictions: No regulated financial services (DFSA licence required separately)
No virtual asset or crypto exchanges
free_zones.restrictions_note: DIFC's Innovation Licence setup guide (January 2025) excludes financial services (for example financial advisory, payment services and crypto or NFT exchanging) and trading or selling physical products, requires a technology activity, and requires physical presence of at least one flexi desk (USD 500 plus VAT per month). The regulated-insurance line is derived from DIFC's regulated-activity framework, not from the guide.

free_zones.name: DIFC (full Financial Services)
free_zones.full_name: Dubai International Financial Centre, regulated financial services

license.notes: Pricing depends on DFSA category and is materially higher than the Innovation Licence. Get a direct quote from DIFC.

banking.notes: Bank acceptance depends on the bank and applicant. No official acceptance rating is published for this zone.

license.notes: JAFZA publishes no price list; its company-formation page points to a cost calculator. No minimum share capital for an FZE or FZCO. Get a quote directly from JAFZA.

office.notes: A lease agreement must be in place at company set-up (JAFZA official page). Facility types include land, warehouses, offices, showrooms and co-working workstations. Founders looking for cheap no-office setups should look at IFZA or Meydan instead.

banking.notes: Large industrial and logistics free zone with broad bank familiarity. DUL coverage is Dubai-wide rather than a special programme limited to selected free zones.

free_zones.name: DHCC

license.notes: Healthcare licenses are sector-specific. Pricing varies. Get a quote directly from DHCC.

banking.notes: Sector-specific. Healthcare banks are comfortable; generalist banks may want extra documentation.

restrictions: Healthcare and wellness focus; supporting commercial activities (e.g. retail, F&B) are also licensed. Clinical facilities and professionals need separate healthcare regulatory licensing.
